nodes.name: MOF Self-Assembly and Annealing
nodes.procedure: Rare earth salts and organic ligands were self-assembled into rod-shaped metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), then carbonized, and in situ adsorbed a Pt precursor for the following high temperature annealing process.

nodes.name: Solution-Phase Synthesis and Reduction
nodes.procedure: Ni_xCeO_{2+x} nanoparticles were grown on the CNTs directly and selectively by solution-phase synthesis, and then, a reductive gas was applied for subsequent surface segregation.
nodes.source_text: Weng et al. obtained nanoscale Ni/CeO2 interfaces on carbon nanotubes (CNTs) by a chemical reduction method.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images of Pt1.5La1.5Ni12/NPC show average metallic particle size of 44 nm dispersed on nanoporous carbon support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average size of metallic particles was 44 nm (Figure 1a), which were dispersed on a nanoporous carbon support.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows PtxY/C leached catalyst particles ranging from 4 to 30 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the catalysts particles were still relatively small, ranging from 4 to 30 nm (Figure 1b) during high temperature treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of PtCe/C-600°C shows nanoparticle size of 4.5-9.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the size of the nanoalloy was substantially larger than Pt particles. This shows an upturn with increasing annealing temperatures, which was at 4.5 - 9.5 nm at 600°C

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of PtCe/C-800°C shows nanoparticle size of 13.5 nm.
HRTEM shows Pt nanoparticles of ~5 nm diameter situated on or embedded in CeO2 support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt nanoparticles were largely situated on the surface of ceria or slightly embedded in the support, and particles' diameters were about 5 nm (Figure 1e and f).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM of Pt5La alloy shows nanoparticles within 6 nm on nanorods.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The wide range of uniformity of the prepared nanoparticles could be found on the nanorods, and the size was within 6 nm (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ni/CeO2 nanoparticles of 4 nm average diameter anchored on CNTs with Ni/Ce ratio close to 1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nanoparticles, with an average diameter of 4 nm, were anchored and distributed on the surface of CNTs, and the bulk Ni/Ce ratio was close to 1:1 (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows PtxY intermetallic particles with crystal size of 2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The prominent features of the final particles were that crystal size was with 2 nm, and this catalyst exhibited a distinctive hydrogen adsorption ability (Figure 1i).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image of Pt3Y nanocatalyst shows particles of 8 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: contributed to a relatively small Pt particles, at 8 nm (Figure 3a).
